headline: S&P 500 fell 2.0% Thursday, a sixth straight loss (Dow -2.2%, Nasdaq -2.3%); over 90% of S&P stocks fell. Anthropic closed its debut 17% above its $83 IPO price but did not lift AI stocks; chips sank, Walmart slipped on its outlook. A December Fed hike is about 95% priced.

sectors.why: No clear sector news. Markets price a 25bp Fed hike in December and the 10-year yield sits near 5.06%, a mild headwind.
No clear US telecom news. Yields above 5% compete with telecom dividends.
Pending home sales fell in October to the lowest since at least 2001 and a December Fed hike is about 95% priced, which weighs on homes, cars and furniture.
Walmart beat on sales (US e-commerce up 23%) but slipped about 1% on its annual outlook. Staples may hold up in a sell-off, but there is no clear direction.
No clear sector news. Jobless claims rose to 203,000 but remain low, so spending looks steady while rate hikes lie ahead.
No clear sector news. Health distributors may feel some pressure from the proposed Medicare audit rule, but the hit is on insurers.
AI chip stocks keep sliding: the chip index fell 2.4% Thursday, Nvidia lost 3.3% (sixth straight drop) and AMD fell 7.7% on a short-seller report. Selling can reverse fast, so confidence is low.
Oil fell earlier in the week on rising US stockpiles, but Middle East supply risk can reverse it quickly; no clear new energy news Thursday.
Higher rates help lending margins, but a 2% market drop, VIX near 28 and a likely December hike weigh on brokers and risk appetite.
The proposed CMS rule widening Medicare Advantage audits (about $90B in recoveries from 2027) still hangs over insurers after this week's 7-13% drops.
No clear sector news for drug and device makers; the Medicare rule targets insurers.
No clear sector news. Higher rates are a mild headwind for project financing.
No clear news for this mixed group.
Gold and miners have sold off this week as the dollar hit a 19-month high and the Fed leans toward more hikes.
No clear sector news. A strong dollar is a mild headwind for chemical exporters.
No clear sector news. A mid-Atlantic factory survey showed slower growth than expected, and rate hikes ahead weigh on capital spending.
Mixed: Target, TJX and Lowe's beat earlier this week, but Walmart's outlook disappointed and Williams-Sonoma fell about 14% on a soft revenue forecast.
Palo Alto rose about 6% on raised 2027 guidance, but AI cloud names CoreWeave (-6%) and Nebius (-9%) fell hard; Anthropic closed its debut 17% above its $83 IPO price.
No clear sector news. Oil is off its highs, which helps fuel costs, but a weak market weighs on cyclicals.
No clear sector news. The 10-year yield eased slightly to about 5.06%, but likely Fed hikes still compete with utility dividends.

avoid.HUM: CMS proposed wider Medicare Advantage audits recovering payments; shares fell 13% and the rule's comment period keeps the risk open.
avoid.UNH: Same CMS Medicare Advantage audit proposal hit UnitedHealth 10%; the final rule outcome is still unknown.
avoid.AMD: Fell 7.7% Thursday after Hunterbrook disclosed a short position, adding a fresh overhang during an AI chip sell-off.
avoid.WSM: Fell about 14% after revenue missed and its 2026 revenue forecast midpoint came in below expectations.
